blocks.text: once addressed the people saying, "O people of Makkah! I have been informed that some of you play a (gambling) game called Nardsheer, whereas Allaah says:

blocks.arabic_text: يٰۤاَيُّهَا الَّذِيْنَ اٰمَنُوْۤا اِنَّمَا الْخَمْرُ وَالْمَيْسِرُ وَالْاَنْصَابُ وَالْاَزْلَامُ رِجْسٌ مِّنْ عَمَلِ الشَّيْطٰنِ فَاجْتَنِبُوْهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُوْنَ
blocks.text: O you who have Imaan! Indeed liquor (wine, beer and other intoxicants), gambling, idols and (distribution by) arrows are filth from the acts of Shaytaan, so abstain from them so that you may be successful (in both worlds).
I swear by Allaah that I shall severely punish him by removing his hair and lashing him. I shall also hand over all his possessions (with him at the time) to the person who brings him in." [^1]
The Lectures of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA)
The Lecture he Delivered in the presence of Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) narrates that after once delivering a short lecture, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Abu Bakr (RA)! Stand up and deliver a lecture." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then delivered a lecture that was shorter than that of Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ then instructed Hadhrat Umar (RA) to deliver a lecture and he complied by delivering a lecture that was shorter than that of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). When Rasulullaah ﷺ then asked another person to deliver a lecture, he was very bombastic in his speech, because of which Rasulullaah ﷺ told him to step down. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "Bombastic speech is from Shaytaan and well delivered speech is magical indeed."
Addressing Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Ibn Ummi Abd! You now deliver a lecture." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) then stood up and after praising Allaah, he said, "O people! Verily Allaah is our Rabb, Islaam is our Deen, the Qur'aan is our Imaam, the Kabah is our Qiblah and (pointing to Rasulullaah ﷺ) this is our Nabi ﷺ. We are pleased with what Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ like for us and we dislike that which Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ dislike for us." To this, Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "Ibn Ummi Abd has spoken well." [^2]

Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Jubayr reports a similar narration from Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) with the addition that Rasulullaah ﷺ also said, "I am pleased with that which Allaah is pleased with for me and for my Ummah and with that which pleases Ibn Ummi Abd. Likewise, I am displeased with that which Allaah is displeased with for me and for my Ummah and with that which displeases Ibn
Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.290) has commented on the chain of narrators.
